findings: Serialize first-time reminder opt-outs with emission. FOR SHARE protects existing preference rows only. An authenticated recipient can save their first opt-out through PUT /api/notifications/preferences after the predicate but before notification insertion. That API performs a direct upsert without the tenant advisory lock, and no notification-insert trigger rechecks preferences. The reminder and audit can therefore commit after the opt-out succeeds. Give preference creation and reminder emission a shared serialization boundary, including the absent-row case.

Preserve decimal accuracy when displaying booked-time differences. domain.ts:16 subtracts fractional booked minutes using binary floating-point arithmetic, while the formatter prints every resulting digit. A legitimate booking lasting 60 minutes 6 seconds produces60.1 booked minutes; a reviewer opening its75-minute report sees0h14.899999999999999min instead of0h14.9min. Use decimal-safe subtraction and formatting, with coverage for fractions such as0.1.
